summary: This informational document registers a media type, application/cellml+xml, for exchanging mathematical models written in CellML 1.0 markup.

eli5.summary: This gives a label that tells a computer a file holds a scientific math model in a certain format, so programs know how to open it.

subtitle: A MIME type for exchanging mathematical models in CellML format

tldr.problem: When exchanging mathematical models described in CellML Umbrella 1.0 format, there was no standard way to label files so software would know they are CellML documents rather than generic XML.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a new MIME type, application/cellml+xml, and registers it with IANA. CellML documents use UTF-8 encoding and typically have a .cellml file extension.
tldr.outcome: Software can now automatically detect and handle CellML documents when they are downloaded or shared, improving interoperability among CellML modeling tools.

today: RFC 4708 is an Informational document and has not been obsoleted. The application/cellml+xml media type remains the official way to label CellML Umbrella 1.0 documents.

sections.title: Why CellML Needs Its Own Media Type
sections.content:
CellML is a standardized markup language for describing mathematical models, especially of biological systems. CellML Umbrella 1.0 is a meta-language that provides a common base for various specific modeling formats.

Although CellML documents are valid XML and contain elements from other specifications like RDF and MathML, these imported elements do not carry enough information on their own to describe a complete model. CellML adds the connective information that ties components together and links them to their metadata. Therefore, CellML documents are more than just a collection of elements from other standards, and require their own MIME type to be properly identified.
sections.eli5: CellML files look like XML files, but they contain special science information that XML alone does not know about. A special label (MIME type) helps software recognize them.

sections.title: The CellML Media Type Registration
sections.content:
The media type is registered as application/cellml+xml. According to RFC 3023, the +xml suffix indicates that the format is based on XML.

CellML Umbrella documents MUST be in UTF-8 encoding. The media type includes an optional charset parameter. If present, it must be set to "utf-8". Software MAY attempt to recover from errors where the charset parameter claims a different encoding, but valid CellML must always be UTF-8.

The recommended file extension for CellML documents is .cellml. Older software may use .xml or the non-standard .cml extension. When a MIME type is available, implementations should open files regardless of extension.
sections.eli5: The official label is application/cellml+xml. The files must be stored in a text format called UTF-8, and should have the .cellml ending. This way, different programs can recognize and open CellML files.

sections.title: Interoperability Considerations
sections.content:
CellML Umbrella documents reference elements from RDF and other XML vocabularies. To properly handle these documents, user agents need more than just XML parsing capability; they require software support for the semantics of RDF and the specific formats used within their CellML instances.

The CellML Umbrella Format Registry lists the specific formats currently supported. Implementers SHOULD support all specific formats listed in this registry, as maintaining the number of specific formats small improves overall interoperability. A range of tools already support CellML, including validators, editors, visualization tools, and systems for translating between related specifications, evaluating mathematics, fitting models to data, and archiving models.
sections.eli5: Different programs need to understand not just the XML structure, but the scientific meanings inside. There is a list of approved CellML variations that programs should all support.

sections.title: Security Concerns with CellML
sections.content:
Because CellML is an XML-based language, it inherits all the security considerations from RFC 3023. Additionally, CellML documents can contain references to external URLs in several ways: XML schema definitions or DTDs, imports of other models, and user-defined data fields.

Some CellML processing software may automatically attempt to retrieve documents from these URLs. This creates security risks. If a CellML document is received by email and opened, the recipient's system could disclose that fact to the sender without the recipient's knowledge. When a document is transferred to a new location, the original author may be notified. Processing software may also make requests on the recipient's behalf, potentially executing actions with the recipient's privileges without consent.

CellML processors can mitigate these threats by requiring explicit user confirmation before loading any external documents, especially in environments where this is a concern.
sections.eli5: A math model file can contain links to other files on the internet. A program opening the file might secretly download those files and tell someone online that you looked at the model. This is risky, so programs should ask you first before fetching anything.

sections.title: Registration with IANA
sections.content:
This document specifies a new media type for IANA registration. The media type name is application, the subtype is cellml+xml, and there are no mandatory parameters. The charset parameter is optional and handled the same way as for application/xml.

The magic number for identifying CellML documents is that they are XML documents with a document element having the local name "model". The intended usage is COMMON, indicating that this media type is expected to be widely used.

The CellML Umbrella 1.0 specification will not change, but the specification defines a process for registering new specific formats. Control over the CellML Umbrella Format Registry is held by the Bioengineering Institute at The University of Auckland, with input from the broader CellML Community.
sections.eli5: IANA is the organization that keeps the official list of all media types. This RFC asks them to add cellml+xml to that list. The registry is controlled by the University of Auckland.
